passage1.text: We're eating more fish than ever these days. At around 20 kilograms per person global fish consumption is now more than twice what it was in the 1960s. What's really remarkable, though, is where that fish comes from. For the first time in human history, most of our aquatic (水产的) food now comes from farming rather than fishing. People ate around 73 million tonnes of farmed fish-just more than half of the volume of fish that humans consumed--in 2014. That's out of a total fish supply of 167 million tonnes; the remaining 20million or so tonnes go into things like animal feed and medical products. To keep eating fish at the current rate, we're definitely going to need to keep aquaculture (水产养 殖) developing. That's because the volume of fish caught in the wild has leveled off since the 1990s. Back in 1974, only 10% of marine fish stocks had been overfished. Now, more than three-tenths are. Only a tenth of our oceans' fish stocks could sustain heavier fishing than current levels. But while catchings at sea have suffered, fish-farming has been growing at a fast rate. A lot of that is coming from China, which produces 60% of the world's farmed fish. In fact, some 35 countries, including China, now produce more farmed than wild-caught fish. This shift toward aquaculture isn't just good for ensuring salmon (三文鱼) on your plate; it's also crucial to ensuring food security and sustainability. By 2050, the world will need to feed an estimated 9.7billion people. They'll have to get their protein somewhere. However, raising cattle, pigs, and other land-based animals requires vast sums of grain and water. For example, pound for pound, beef requires 15 times more feed to raise than carp, a freshwater fish farmed all over Asia. That grain-and the water needed to grow it-could be consumed by people instead. However, aquaculture is no silver bullet. In some southeast Asian countries, shrimp farming does disastrous damage to marine ecosystems. Despite these problems, however, shrimp continues to be among the most popular seafoods worldwide.

passage2.text: In 2020, the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the World Food Programme (WFP). Why a Nobel Prize for the WFP, and why now? In 2019, the WFP assisted nearly 100 million people in 88 countries. It is the safety net for those who fall off the edge of existence. It is a response to solving the problem of food instability. Its Nobel Prize reminds us all of the moral hazard in imagining that the poor and vulnerable are somebody else's problem. The WFP has been around since 1961 and has been the global coordinator of nationally based efforts to avoid disasters with food aid. Despite decades of effort to eliminate hunger, the latest estimate is that about 11% of people on the planet (about 820 million people) are suffering daily undernourishment. Progress at reducing undernourishment has stopped despite gains through the 1990s and 2000s. Developed countries sometimes offer food and aid to developing ones, but at a price. One American philosopher stated that addressing the needs of the poor and vulnerable is about more than money-it is mostly about creating conditions under which prosperity and opportunity can thrive. When aid is offered with heavy conditions, attached, like loan repayment or food for resources, it often widens the gap between rich and poor and sustains the old world order. This is why the work of the WFP is so vital. The scientific community, however, can provide a helping hand to the WFP. By sharing knowledge of agriculture and climate with peers in countries most vulnerable to poverty and hunger, scientists can help reduce these problems. By making its voice heard, science can lead by example. The ability to overcome food shortages that must be built into some of the poorest countries will not come from loans from wealthy countries, which may have food problems of their own, or world economic institutions. This ability will be built upon self-confident people using open and shared scientific knowledge to pull themselves out of their misery.

paragraphs.A: Not doing something will always be faster than doing it. This philosophy applies in many areas of life. For example, there is no meeting that goes faster than not having a meeting at all. This is not to say you should never attend another meeting, but the truth is that we say "yes" to too many things we don't actually want to do.
paragraphs.B: How often do people ask you to do something and you just reply, "Sure." Three days later, you're overwhelmed by how much is on your to-do list. We become frustrated by our obligations even though we were the ones who said "yes" to them in the first place. Even worse, people will occasionally fight to do things that waste time. You don't have to do something just because it exists. It's worth asking if things are necessary. Many of them are not, and a simple "no" will be more productive than whatever work the most efficient person can cope with. But if the benefits of saying "no" are so obvious, then why do we say "yes" so often?
paragraphs.C: We say "yes" to many requests not because we want to do them, but because we don't want to be seen as rude or unhelpful. Often, we have to consider saying "no" to someone we will interact with again in the future-our co-worker, our spouse, our family and friends. Saying "no" to our superiors at work can be particularly difficult. In these situations, I like the approach recommended in Essentialism by Greg McKeown. He writes, "Remind your superiors what you would be neglecting if you said 'yes' and force them to deal with the trade-off. For example, if your manager comes to you and asks you to do X, you can respond with ‘Yes, I'm happy to make this the priority. Which of these other projects should I deprioritize to pay attention to this new project?’"
paragraphs.D: Collaborating with others is an important element of life. The thought of straining the relationship outweighs the commitment of our time and energy. For this reason, it can be helpful to be gracious in your response. Do whatever favors you can, and be warm-hearted and direct when you have to say no. But even after we have accounted for these social considerations, many of us still seem to do a poor job of managing the trade-off between yes and no. We find ourselves over-committed to things that don't meaningfully improve or support those around us, and certainly don't improve our own lives.
paragraphs.E: Perhaps one issue is how we think about the meaning of yes and no. The words "yes" and "no" get so often used in comparison with each other that it feels like they carry equal weight in conversation. In reality, they're not just opposite in meaning, but of entirely different magnitudes in commitment. When you say "no", you're only saying "no" to one option. When you say "yes", you're saying "no" to every other option. I like how economist Tim Harford put it, "Every time we say ‘yes’ to a request, we're also saying 'no' to anything else we might accomplish with the time." Once you're committed to something, you've already decided how that future block of time will be spent. In other words, saying "no" saves you time in the future. Saying "yes" costs you time in the future. "No" is a form of time credit. You retain the ability to spend your future time however you want. "Yes" is a form of time debt. You have to pay back your commitment at some point.
paragraphs.F: "No" is a decision. "Yes" is a responsibility. Saying "no" is sometimes seen as a luxury that only those in power can afford. And it's true: turning down opportunities is easier when you can fall back on the safety net provided by power, money, and authority. But it's also true that saying "no" is not merely a privilege reserved for the successful. It's also a strategy that can help you become successful. Saying "no" is an important skill to develop at any stage of your career because it retains the most important asset in life: your time. As investor Pedro Sorrentino put it, "If you don't guard your time, people will steal it from you." You need to say "no" to whatever isn't leading you toward your goals.
paragraphs.G: Nobody embodied this idea better than Steve Jobs, who said, "People think focus means saying ‘yes’ to the thing you've got to focus on. But that's not what it means at all. It means saying 'no' to the hundred other good ideas that there are. You have to pick carefully." Jobs had another great quote about saying "no": "I'm actually as proud of the things we haven't done as the things I have done. Innovation is saying 'no' to 1,000 things."
paragraphs.H: Over time, as you continue to improve and succeed, your strategy needs to change. The opportunity cost of your time increases as you become more successful. At first, you just eliminate the obvious distractions and explore the rest. As your skills improve and you learn to separate what works from what doesn't, you have to continually increase your threshold for saying "yes". You still need to say "no” to distractions, but you also need to learn to say "no" to opportunities that were previously good uses of time, so you can make space for better uses of time. It's a good problem to have, but it can be a tough skill to master.
paragraphs.I: What is true about health is also true about productivity: an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. More effort is wasted doing things that don't matter than is wasted doing things inefficiently. And if that is the case, elimination is a more useful skill than optimization. I'm reminded of the famous Peter Drucker quote, "There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all."

questions.script:
Summer doesn't begin for two more days, but scientists are already sounding the alarm about dangerous ice melts going on right now in Greenland.
The vast island usually locks away enough fresh water in its ice sheet, which if melted can raise global sea levels by six meters. And research shows that in recent years its ice has melted faster than ever before. This month, as temperatures in northwestern Greenland approach all-time highs, researchers are encountering unusual, surprising levels of melting ice in the region.
The most significant concern here is how early this is all happening. Greenland experiences annual ice melt and growth cycles. But this year, the melting season began in early May. That's a month earlier than normal and something that's happened only once before in the historical record in 2016.
That means that not only is the ice melting very fast, it has more time to melt this summer than it would in a normal climate system. Longer melt seasons like this one seem to lead to much greater contributions to sea-level rise than in previous decades.

questions.script:
Bundles containing thousands of pounds in cash keep turning up on the streets of Blackhall Colliery in northern England, according to police. Residents of the village have been coming across bundles of £20 notes—usually worth £2,000—in the former mining village in County Durham.
The latest discovery was on Monday, meaning four of these cash bundles have been handed in this year and 13 since 2014.
The bundles are usually left in plain sight and have been scattered across the small coastal village. The owner has two weeks to collect the cash, which is then returned to the finder if not claimed, according to Peterlee Police.
A Durham Police spokesperson said the money has been returned to the lucky finders in all cases except yesterday.
Policeman John Forster said in a statement: "The circumstances remain a mystery so we would welcome any information that will help us get to the bottom of these random incidents."
He told The Northern Echo: "It isn't an affluent part of the world, so for them to find cash of that amount and instantly think about taking it to the police stations shows the community spirit there is."

questions.script:
W: It's your birthday next week. What have you got planned?
M: I'm not sure. I often feel strange on my birthday. It's like my brain decides to have a crisis.
W: It's not entirely unusual to feel anxious or sad around your birthday. Birthdays can tap into a lot of things people worry about, including their achievements in life in the past decade, or their accomplishments of the past year. Many begin to search for the meaning of their existence, leading to behaviors such as ending or starting a relationship, or plans, like starting a vigorous diet or fitness program.
M: I have wonderful friends and I love celebrating their birthdays. But I don't like being the center of attention, receiving gifts and having a fuss made. It seems to trigger a type of social anxiety. I think social media too can intensify things as birthdays now play out more publicly. Birthday reminders can be helpful, but I kind of worry I won't be able to drum up my own day and show it to look as exciting as it is supposed to be.
W: Well, to deal with the birthday blues, you should not isolate yourself. It's best to gradually face your birthday with people you trust. That would help you learn self-acceptance, or that it's okay to be the focus.
M: Perhaps. Or I could perceive my birthday as an opportunity to do something for others like asking people to make a donation instead of buying a gift.
W: Exactly. Or even simply see your birthday as an opportunity to bring people together for them to have fun.

questions.script:
Steve Miller began his career in IT back in the late 1980s. Being a deaf person in tech required a huge amount of effort in organization. Because there was no email or text message service, everything had to be done face to face, or by telephone. Communicating in meetings was very difficult. He needed a sign language interpreter for every meeting, but it was a huge effort to coordinate.
These days, although challenges still remain, it's a good time to be a deaf person in tech, says Miller. Big advances in speech recognition technology have enabled communication tools to turn live speech into text in real time on your smartphone or laptop, and sign language into text as well.
New Tech coupled with improvements in hearing aid technology and medical advances means that Miller is able to focus far more on his work. He has benefited to a great extent from a tiny hearing device in his ear. It gives him a degree of hearing, and he can use a variety of communication methods depending on the situation. He can employ lip-reading and have meetings via video instead of on the phone. These things have made a huge difference. He no longer has to worry about whether or not he can understand. He can just concentrate on how interesting the meeting might be and what he needs to get out of it in order to progress.

Don't go for a colour because it's in fashion, or you've seen it in a magazine.
If you're weary of full colour, test your tolerance with smaller spaces, such as the inside of a cupboard or a bright window frame. If it gives you joy every time you open the cupboard, you can start to take it further.
One can also paint the wooden frameworks the same colour as the walls, helping the rooms look bigger. In the kitchen, painting the overhead cupboards and the walls in the same colour can make it feel more spacious.
While painting the kitchen counters, a bold colour can make everything feel more open and lighter. Additionally, a painted ceiling is a magical thing without being too obvious and can affect how the space feels as well.

options.A: Children must read at least 3 times a week.
options.B: Reading is a habit every child can develop.

questions.script:
Parents often hear that reading to their children is critical for supporting development, and the message is getting through to them. In fact, in the United States, a little over half of children between the ages of three and five were read to every day in 2007, and 83% of children in that age group in the same country were read to three or more times per week in 2012.
This is good news, because reading to young children helps their language and brain development. In fact, recent research has found that both the quality and quantity of shared book reading in infancy predicted later childhood vocabulary and reading skills. In other words, the more time parents spend reading, the greater the developmental benefits in their four-year-old children.
This is an important finding. But does it matter what books parents read? A new study has investigated this question. It followed infants across the second six months of life and found that when parents showed babies books that had faces or objects with specific labels, they learned more. This is in contrast to books that did not name images, or books that had the same label under each image. Books that named different characters also promoted greater learning. So what does this mean for parents? Not all books are created equal, so parents need to choose the books they share with their children with great care.

So what does this mean for parents? Not all books are created equal, so parents need to choose the books they share with their children with great care.
questions.expl: Choose carefully what to read to their children. 详解：事实细节题。短文最后提到“Not all books are created equal, so parents need to choose the books they share with their children with great care.”，即并非所有书都一样，父母需要谨慎选择与孩子分享的书。选项B与原文建议一致，故答案为B。 涉及知识点：听力中总结性建议（need to choose...with great care）的定位、同义替换（choose carefully 与 choose...with great care）。

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.expl: involving 详解：语法判断：空格前的“The research examined three studies”是完整主谓宾结构，空格后是名词短语“more than 18,000 participants”，因此本空需填入动词-ing形式，与名词短语共同修饰“studies”。语义判断：空格所在句意为“这项研究调查了3项____1.8万多名参与者的研究”，结合句意，3项研究应“包括、涉及”1.8万多名参与者，备选动词-ing形式中“involving”（涉及）符合语义，“composing”（组成）需与of连用（be composed of），故排除，答案为K。 涉及知识点：动词-ing形式作定语、动词辨析（involving 与 composing 的用法区别）。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：句子缺少谓语动词，空格前有be动词的过去式was，空格后是介词with，因此本空需填入动词的过去分词形式，构成被动语态或固定搭配。语义判断：空格所在句意为“在这3项研究中，相较于母亲，对父亲来说，养育孩子与更多积极的幸福效果____”，“be associated with”为固定搭配，意为“与……有关”，代入句中符合语义，其他备选词无法与with构成合理搭配，故答案为B。 涉及知识点：固定搭配（be associated with）、动词过去分词的用法。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.expl: note 详解：语法判断：空格前是名词复数“the authors”，空格后是that引导的宾语从句，句子缺少谓语动词，且主语为复数，谓语需用动词原形。语义判断：空格所在句意为“在一项研究中，作者们____，父亲在照顾孩子和陪伴孩子时，更有可能把‘玩要’作为一项活动”，备选动词原形中“note”（指出、注意到）代入句中符合语义，即作者们指出某一现象，故答案为L。 涉及知识点：主谓一致（复数主语接动词原形）、动词辨析（note 的语义用法）。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：空格前有不定冠词an，空格后有名词activity，因此本空需填入以元音音素开头的形容词，修饰activity。语义判断：空格所在句意为“父亲在照顾孩子和陪伴孩子时，更有可能把‘玩要’作为一项____活动”，备选形容词中“additional”（额外的）代入句中符合语义，即玩耍是除照顾孩子外的额外活动；“associated”（有关联的）虽以元音音素开头，但语义不符，故答案为A。 涉及知识点：形容词修饰名词、以元音音素开头的形容词辨析。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.expl: cultivate 详解：语法判断：空格所在短语与“experience positive feelings”构成并列结构，空格前有不定式符号to（offer opportunities to do），因此本空需填入动词原形，与experience对应。语义判断：空格所在句意为“和孩子一起玩可能会给父母提供体验积极情感的机会，并____与孩子的亲密关系”，备选动词原形中“cultivate”（培养）代入句中符合语义，即培养亲密关系，故答案为D。 涉及知识点：并列结构中的动词一致、动词辨析（cultivate 的语义用法）。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：空格前有fewer，空格后有名词symptoms，因此本空需填入形容词，修饰symptoms。语义判断：空格所在句意为“父亲也比没有孩子的男性更好，他们更幸福，生活满意度更高，____症状更少”，结合句意，此处应填入表达负面情绪的形容词，备选形容词中“depressive”（抑郁的）符合语义，即抑郁症状更少，其他形容词无此含义，故答案为E。 涉及知识点：形容词修饰名词、情感类形容词辨析（depressive 的语义）。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.expl: however 详解：语法判断：空格所在句句子成分完整（主谓宾结构），因此本空需填入副词，修饰整个句子或体现逻辑关系。语义判断：前文提到“父亲比没有孩子的男性更幸福”，本句指出“对于母亲来说，与没有孩子的女性相比，结果就不那么乐观了”，前后为转折关系，备选副词中“however”（然而）体现转折，其他副词无此含义，故答案为H。 涉及知识点：副词的逻辑功能（转折关系）、副词辨析（however 的用法）。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.expl: emotions 详解：语法判断：and连接两个并列成分“greater trouble”和“fewer positive____”，空格前有fewer（修饰可数名词复数），因此本空需填入可数名词复数，与trouble对应。语义判断：空格所在句意为“妈妈们说她们拥有更大的自主权，但也有‘更多的麻烦’和更少的积极____”，备选名词中“emotions”（情绪）代入句中符合语义，即更少的积极情绪，故答案为G。 涉及知识点：并列结构中的名词一致、可数名词复数的用法。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.expl: directly 详解：语法判断：空格所在句句子成分完整（主谓宾结构），空格将动词短语“engaging in”分隔开，因此本空需填入副词，修饰动词engaging。语义判断：空格所在句意为“与其他经历相比，妈妈们在与孩子互动时的情绪更快乐，但在____照顾孩子时则不然”，备选副词中“directly”（直接地）代入句中符合语义，即直接照顾孩子时情绪不佳，故答案为F。 涉及知识点：副词修饰动词、副词辨析（directly 的语义用法）。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.expl: 详解：语法判断：空格前有谓语动词have和形容词important，空格后有介词for，因此本空需填入名词。语义判断：空格所在句意为“这种差异表明，父母如何花时间陪伴孩子可能对父母的幸福有重要____”，备选名词中“implications”（影响、含意）代入句中符合语义，即对幸福有重要影响，故答案为I。 涉及知识点：名词作宾语、语义辨析（implications 的语义）。

questions.stem: 36. People often grant a request just because they want to appear polite and helpful.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“grant a request”“polite and helpful”定位到文章C)段第一句。精析：同义转述题。定位句提到“We say 'yes' to many requests not because we want to do them, but because we don't want to be seen as rude or unhelpful.”，即我们答应许多请求不是因为想去做，而是不想被认为没礼貌或不愿助人。题干中的“grant a request”对应“say 'yes' to many requests”，“polite and helpful”对应“don't want to be seen as rude or unhelpful”，故答案为C。 涉及知识点：同义转述、定位关键词（grant a request, polite, helpful）的提取。

questions.stem: 37. It's no easy job learning to say "no" to opportunities that were once considered worth grasping.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“no easy job”“once considered worth grasping”定位到H)段最后两句。精析：细节归纳题。定位句提到“You still need to say 'no' to distractions, but you also need to learn to say 'no' to opportunities that were previously good uses of time... it can be a tough skill to master.”，即需要学会对以前认为是很好利用时间的机会说“不”，这是一项很难掌握的技能。题干中的“say 'no' to opportunities that were once considered worth grasping”对应“say 'no' to opportunities that were previously good uses of time”，“no easy job”对应“tough”，题干是对定位句的归纳，故答案为H。 涉及知识点：细节归纳、同义替换（previously good uses of time 与 once considered worth grasping）。

questions.stem: 38. When you decline a request, you are saving your future time.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“decline a request”“saving your future time”定位到E)段第八句。精析：同义转述题。定位句提到“saying 'no' saves you time in the future”，即说“不”可以节省未来的时间。题干中的“decline a request”对应“saying 'no'”，“saving your future time”与原文一致，故答案为E。 涉及知识点：同义转述、定位关键词（saving your future time）的匹配。

questions.stem: 39. People sometimes struggle to do things that are simply a waste of time.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“struggle”“a waste of time”定位到B)段第四句。精析：同义转述题。定位句提到“people will occasionally fight to do things that waste time”，即人们偶尔会勉强自己做浪费时间的事。题干中的“struggle”对应“fight”，“a waste of time”与原文一致，故答案为B。 涉及知识点：同义替换（fight 与 struggle）、定位关键词（a waste of time）的匹配。

questions.stem: 40. Doing efficiently what is not worth doing is the most useless effort.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“not worth doing”“the most useless effort”定位到I)段最后一句。精析：同义转述题。定位句提到“there is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all”，即高效地做根本不该做的事是最无用的。题干中的“not worth doing”对应“which should not be done at all”，“the most useless effort”对应“nothing so useless”，故答案为I。 涉及知识点：同义转述、名言类信息的理解与匹配。

questions.stem: 41. It is especially difficult for people to decline to do what their superiors ask them to do.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“especially difficult”“decline”“superiors”定位到C)段第三句。精析：同义转述题。定位句提到“Saying 'no' to our superiors at work can be particularly difficult”，即工作中对上司说“不”可能尤其困难。题干中的“especially difficult”对应“particularly difficult”，“decline to do what their superiors ask them to do”对应“Saying 'no' to our superiors”，故答案为C。 涉及知识点：同义替换（particularly 与 especially, decline 与 saying 'no'）、定位关键词（superiors）的匹配。

questions.stem: 42. People agree to do too many things they are in fact unwilling to do.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“agree”“in fact unwilling”定位到A)段最后一句。精析：细节归纳题。定位句提到“the truth is that we say 'yes' to too many things we don't actually want to do”，即我们对太多实际上不想做的事说“是”。题干中的“agree”对应“say 'yes'”，“in fact unwilling to do”对应“don't actually want to do”，题干是对原文的归纳，故答案为A。 涉及知识点：细节归纳、同义替换（agree 与 say 'yes'）。

questions.stem: 43. According to one famous entrepreneur, innovation means refusal to do an enormous number of things.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“innovation”“refusal”“enormous”定位到G)段最后一句。精析：同义转述题。定位句提到“Innovation is saying 'no' to 1,000 things”，即创新就是对1000件事说“不”。题干中的“innovation means refusal to do an enormous number of things”是对原文的同义转述，故答案为G。 涉及知识点：同义转述、数字（1,000）与泛指（enormous number）的转化。

questions.stem: 44. It is an essential aspect of life to cooperate with other people.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“essential aspect”“cooperate”定位到D)段第一句。精析：同义转述题。定位句提到“Collaborating with others is an important element of life”，即与他人合作是生活的重要组成部分。题干中的“essential aspect”对应“important element”，“cooperate”对应“Collaborating”，故答案为D。 涉及知识点：同义替换（Collaborating 与 cooperate, important element 与 essential aspect）。

questions.stem: 45. Refusing a request is sometimes seen as a privilege not enjoyed by ordinary people.
questions.expl: 定位：由题干中的“Refusing a request”“privilege”定位到F)段第二句。精析：同义转述题。定位句提到“Saying 'no' is sometimes seen as a luxury that only those in power can afford”，即说“不”有时被视为只有当权者才能负担得起的奢侈品。题干中的“privilege”对应“luxury”，“not enjoyed by ordinary people”对应“only those in power can afford”，故答案为F。 涉及知识点：同义替换（luxury 与 privilege, only those in power can afford 与 not enjoyed by ordinary people）。

questions.stem: 46. What does the author say is remarkable about the fish we eat?

options.A: They reproduce quickly.
options.B: They are mostly farmed.
options.C: They have become as important as grain.
options.D: They have a longer history than humans.

questions.expl:
They are mostly farmed. 详解：定位：由题干中的“remarkable about the fish we eat”定位到第一段最后一句和第二段。精析：细节辨认题。第一段最后一句提到“真正值得注意的是这些鱼的来源”，第二段接着指出“我们大部分的水产食物来自养殖而非捕捞”。选项B与原文表述一致，故答案为B。避错：文中未提及鱼的繁殖速度（
A）、与谷物的重要性对比（
C）及鱼的历史（
D），均排除。 涉及知识点：细节辨认、段落间逻辑关系（引出话题—具体说明）的理解。

questions.stem: 47. What do we need to do if we keep consuming fish at the current rate?

options.A: Increase the fishing volume considerably.
options.B: Develop more advanced fishing technology.
options.C: Enlarge the marine fish stocks effectively.
options.D: Expand the scale of fish-farming continuously.

questions.expl: 详解：定位：由题干中的“keep consuming fish at the current rate”定位到第四段第一句。精析：推理判断题。定位句提到“为了保证鱼肉摄入量一直处于现如今的水平，我们肯定需要让水产养殖业不断发展”，“不断发展水产养殖业”必然包括扩大养殖规模，选项D符合推断，故答案为D。避错：A、B均涉及捕捞，与原文强调的“养殖”方向不符；文中未提及扩大海洋鱼类数量（C），均排除。 涉及知识点：推理判断、核心概念（aquaculture 水产养殖）的理解。

questions.stem: 48. What does the author say about China in terms of aquatic food?

options.A: It places increasing emphasis on fishing now.
options.B: It boasts of the world's largest fishing stocks.
options.C: It raises more fish than caught from the wild.
options.D: It supplies 60% of the world's fish products.

questions.expl: It raises more fish than caught from the wild. 详解：定位：由题干中的“China”“aquatic food”定位到第六段最后一句。精析：细节辨认题。定位句指出“包括中国在内的约35个国家，现如今的养殖鱼产量超过了野生捕捞量”，选项C中的“raises more fish than caught from the wild”与“produce more farmed than wild-caught”为同义替换，故答案为C。避错：A与原文“养殖为主”的大意不符；B文中未提及“中国拥有世界最多渔业资源”；D混淆“养殖鱼产量占全球60%”与“提供世界60%的鱼肉产品”，均排除。 涉及知识点：细节辨认、同义替换（farmed 与 raises, wild-caught 与 caught from the wild）。

questions.stem: 49. Why does the author say aquaculture is so important these days?

options.A: It is a must for feeding the world's fast-growing population.
options.B: It proves a reliable source of protein for humans and animals.
options.C: It is essential to maintaining both mental and physical health.
options.D: It ensures a balanced healthy diet for people the world over.

questions.expl:
详解：定位：由题干中的“aquaculture is so important”定位到倒数第二段。精析：推理判断题。定位段提到“这种向水产养殖的转变对于确保食品安全性和可持续性至关重要”，并指出2050年全球需养活97亿人，而养鱼比养陆地动物更节省资源（谷物、水）。由此可推断，水产养殖对养活快速增长的人口至关重要，选项A符合推断，故答案为A。避错：文中未提及水产养殖为动物提供蛋白质（
B）、对身心健康的影响（
C）及确保饮食平衡（
D），均排除。 涉及知识点：推理判断、因果关系（人口增长需求—水产养殖的重要性）的理解。

questions.stem: 50. What does the author imply by saying aquaculture is no silver bullet?

options.A: Shrimp-farming is a risky business.
options.B: Fish-farming will not be sustainable.
options.C: Fish-farming may cause serious problems too.
options.D: Shrimp-farming can become quite expensive.

questions.expl: Fish-farming may cause serious problems too. 详解：定位：由题干中的“aquaculture is no silver bullet”定位到最后一段。精析：细节辨认题。定位句后提到“在一些东南亚国家，虾类养殖对海洋生态造成了灾难性的破坏”，即水产养殖并非万能，也存在负面影响，选项C符合题意，故答案为C。避错：A“养虾有风险”、D“养虾会变贵”文中未提及；B“水产养殖不可持续”与原文“确保可持续性”矛盾，均排除。 涉及知识点：细节辨认、习语理解（no silver bullet 并非万能良方）。

questions.stem: 51. What does the WFP's winning of the Nobel Peace Prize make us realize?

options.A: More and more people in the world are suffering from starvation.
options.B: All of us can be affected by food instability one way or another.
options.C: It is hazardous to leave millions of people poor and vulnerable.
options.D: It is morally wrong to think helping the poor is not our business.

questions.expl: It is morally wrong to think helping the poor is not our business. 详解：定位：由题干中的“WFP's winning of the Nobel Peace Prize”定位到第二段最后一句。精析：细节辨认题。定位句提到“它的诺贝尔奖提醒我们所有人，把穷人和弱势群体当成别人的问题是一种道德危机”，选项D中的“morally wrong”对应“moral hazard”，“think helping the poor is not our business”对应“imagining that the poor and vulnerable are somebody else's problem”，故答案为D。避错：A“越来越多人挨饿”文中未提及“越来越多”；B“所有人都受粮食不稳定影响”文中未提及；C“让数百万人贫困弱势是危险的”与原文“道德危机”不符，均排除。 涉及知识点：细节辨认、同义替换（moral hazard 与 morally wrong）。

questions.stem: 52. What do we learn about the WFP's effort to eliminate hunger?

options.A: It has ensured a sufficient food supply to millions.
options.B: It is still far from its goal despite the progress made.
options.C: It has done a good job in combating natural disasters.
options.D: It is preventing starvation occurring on a global scale.

questions.expl: It is still far from its goal despite the progress made. 详解：定位：由题干中的“WFP's effort to eliminate hunger”定位到第三段。精析：推理判断题。定位段提到“世界粮食计划署自1961年成立以来一直致力于通过粮食援助避免灾难，尽管付出了几十年努力，但约11%的人仍营养不良，减少营养不良的进展已停止”。由此可推断，尽管取得了一些进展，但距离消除饥饿的目标仍很远，选项B符合推断，故答案为B。避错：A“确保数百万人粮食充足”表述绝对，文中未提及；C“抗击自然灾害”文中未提及；D“阻止全球饥荒”文中未提及，均排除。 涉及知识点：推理判断、转折关系（despite 引导的让步状语）的理解。

questions.stem: 53. What will happen when food aid is offered at a price?

options.A: The rich will become richer and the poor poorer.
options.B: More people will be willing to join in the effort.
options.C: More food will be made available to the needy.
options.D: The relief effort will be rendered less sustainable.

questions.expl: The rich will become richer and the poor poorer. 详解：定位：由题干中的“food aid is offered at a price”定位到第四段倒数第二句。精析：细节辨认题。定位句提到“如果援助附带沉重的条件，如偿还贷款或以粮食换资源，这往往会扩大贫富差距”，选项A“富人更富，穷人更穷”是“扩大贫富差距”的同义表述，故答案为A。避错：B“更多人愿意参与”、C“更多食物提供给有需要的人”、D“救济工作难以为继”文中均未提及，均排除。 涉及知识点：细节辨认、同义替换（widen the gap between rich and poor 与 The rich will become richer and the poor poorer）。

questions.stem: 54. How can scientists help cope with poverty and hunger?

options.A: By collaborating closely with world economic institutions.
options.B: By sharing expertise with peers in poverty-stricken nations.
options.C: By setting up more food research programs in developing countries.
options.D: By building self-respect in people suffering from undernutrition.

questions.expl: By sharing expertise with peers in poverty-stricken nations. 详解：定位：由题干中的“scientists help cope with poverty and hunger”定位到第五段第二句。精析：推理判断题。定位句提到“通过与最容易遭受贫困和饥饿的国家的同行分享农业和气候知识，科学家可以帮助减少这些问题”，选项B中的“expertise”对应“knowledge of agriculture and climate”，“poverty-stricken nations”对应“countries most vulnerable to poverty and hunger”，故答案为B。避错：A“与世界经济机构密切合作”文中未提及，且合作对象并非科学家；C“在发展中国家建立更多食品研究项目”文中未提及；D“在营养不良的人身上建立自尊”文中未提及，均排除。 涉及知识点：推理判断、同义替换（knowledge 与 expertise, vulnerable to poverty and hunger 与 poverty-stricken）。

questions.stem: 55. What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage?

options.A: Wealthy nations should solve their own food problems first.
options.B: Rich countries should be more generous in providing food aid.
options.C: Poor nations should enhance their own ability to solve their food shortages.
options.D: World economic institutions should play a bigger role in fighting hunger.

questions.expl: Poor nations should enhance their own ability to solve their food shortages. 详解：定位：由题干中的“at the end of the passage”定位到最后一段最后一句。精析：推理判断题。定位句提到“一些最贫穷的国家必须具备克服粮食短缺的能力，这种能力将建立在自信的人们利用开放和共享的科学知识使自己摆脱痛苦的基础上”。由此可推断，作者认为贫穷国家应提高自己解决粮食短缺的能力，选项C符合推断，故答案为C。避错：A“富裕国家应先解决自身粮食问题”文中未提及；B“富裕国家应更慷慨提供粮食援助”文中未提及；D“世界经济机构应发挥更大作用”文中未提及，均排除。 涉及知识点：推理判断、段落主旨（贫穷国家自身能力建设的重要性）的理解。

Summer doesn't begin for two more days, but scientists are already sounding the alarm about dangerous ice melts going on right now in Greenland.
The vast island usually locks away enough fresh water in its ice sheet, which if melted can raise global sea levels by six meters. And research shows that in recent years its ice has melted faster than ever before. This month, as temperatures in northwestern Greenland approach all-time highs, researchers are encountering unusual, surprising levels of melting ice in the region.
The most significant concern here is how early this is all happening. Greenland experiences annual ice melt and growth cycles. But this year, the melting season began in early May. That's a month earlier than normal and something that's happened only once before in the historical record in 2016.
That means that not only is the ice melting very fast, it has more time to melt this summer than it would in a normal climate system. Longer melt seasons like this one seem to lead to much greater contributions to sea-level rise than in previous decades.

Bundles containing thousands of pounds in cash keep turning up on the streets of Blackhall Colliery in northern England, according to police. Residents of the village have been coming across bundles of £20 notes—usually worth £2,000—in the former mining village in County Durham.
The latest discovery was on Monday, meaning four of these cash bundles have been handed in this year and 13 since 2014.
The bundles are usually left in plain sight and have been scattered across the small coastal village. The owner has two weeks to collect the cash, which is then returned to the finder if not claimed, according to Peterlee Police.
A Durham Police spokesperson said the money has been returned to the lucky finders in all cases except yesterday.
Policeman John Forster said in a statement: "The circumstances remain a mystery so we would welcome any information that will help us get to the bottom of these random incidents."
He told The Northern Echo: "It isn't an affluent part of the world, so for them to find cash of that amount and instantly think about taking it to the police stations shows the community spirit there is."

W: It's your birthday next week. What have you got planned?
M: I'm not sure. I often feel strange on my birthday. It's like my brain decides to have a crisis.
W: It's not entirely unusual to feel anxious or sad around your birthday. Birthdays can tap into a lot of things people worry about, including their achievements in life in the past decade, or their accomplishments of the past year. Many begin to search for the meaning of their existence, leading to behaviors such as ending or starting a relationship, or plans, like starting a vigorous diet or fitness program.
M: I have wonderful friends and I love celebrating their birthdays. But I don't like being the center of attention, receiving gifts and having a fuss made. It seems to trigger a type of social anxiety. I think social media too can intensify things as birthdays now play out more publicly. Birthday reminders can be helpful, but I kind of worry I won't be able to drum up my own day and show it to look as exciting as it is supposed to be.
W: Well, to deal with the birthday blues, you should not isolate yourself. It's best to gradually face your birthday with people you trust. That would help you learn self-acceptance, or that it's okay to be the focus.
M: Perhaps. Or I could perceive my birthday as an opportunity to do something for others like asking people to make a donation instead of buying a gift.
W: Exactly. Or even simply see your birthday as an opportunity to bring people together for them to have fun.

W: The metro was absolutely terrible this morning.
M: Oh, was there a delay?
W: No, but the train was so packed that I could barely move, and it was difficult to breathe too. At every station, more people squeezed in and I got pushed further and further inside. When I got to my station, I could hardly get out. Once I did get out, I was totally exhausted.
M: That sounds like a nightmare. Why didn't you take the bus?
W: The bus takes twice as long and it's just as crowded.
M: Well, what's the alternative? Haven't you got a car?
W: I've got a driver's license, but that's all. I'm saving up to buy something reasonably small and cute, but it's still a bit expensive for me, and it'll take a while before I have enough money.
M: Have you thought about getting an electric motorbike?
W: I consider that for maybe a minute. But honestly, I've just seen too many horrible accidents involving those dangerous monsters.
M: What about those popular shared bikes? You could register to use one.
W: Yeah, that's a possibility. There are always several of those bikes out in front of our apartment complex.
M: Or you could just walk to work.
W: Well, it's five kilometers from home to the office. But you've given me a thought. I could take a change of clothes and jog to work. But at this time of year, the air pollution is a real problem.
M: Oh, yeah. I didn't think of that. You take a taxi if you really have to.
W: Well, that's an expensive way to get to work.
M: Not if you use a ride sharing app.
W: Good idea. I'll download one immediately. Thank you.

Steve Miller began his career in IT back in the late 1980s. Being a deaf person in tech required a huge amount of effort in organization. Because there was no email or text message service, everything had to be done face to face, or by telephone. Communicating in meetings was very difficult. He needed a sign language interpreter for every meeting, but it was a huge effort to coordinate.
These days, although challenges still remain, it's a good time to be a deaf person in tech, says Miller. Big advances in speech recognition technology have enabled communication tools to turn live speech into text in real time on your smartphone or laptop, and sign language into text as well.
New Tech coupled with improvements in hearing aid technology and medical advances means that Miller is able to focus far more on his work. He has benefited to a great extent from a tiny hearing device in his ear. It gives him a degree of hearing, and he can use a variety of communication methods depending on the situation. He can employ lip-reading and have meetings via video instead of on the phone. These things have made a huge difference. He no longer has to worry about whether or not he can understand. He can just concentrate on how interesting the meeting might be and what he needs to get out of it in order to progress.

Colour is now spreading through our homes, up staircases, across wood frames and ceilings, filling in neutral spaces.
According to one interior designer, when people return home, they want to see colours that cheer them up and give them a hug. Pure white walls simply don't do that. They don't look after you.
Another interior designer commented that certain combinations can key into something on a deeper level, transporting you to a different moment in time. That's the power of colour.
If you are thinking to try colour on some of your neutral walls, the advice is refreshingly simple: Choose a colour you actually like.
Don't go for a colour because it's in fashion, or you've seen it in a magazine.
If you're weary of full colour, test your tolerance with smaller spaces, such as the inside of a cupboard or a bright window frame. If it gives you joy every time you open the cupboard, you can start to take it further.
One can also paint the wooden frameworks the same colour as the walls, helping the rooms look bigger. In the kitchen, painting the overhead cupboards and the walls in the same colour can make it feel more spacious.
While painting the kitchen counters, a bold colour can make everything feel more open and lighter. Additionally, a painted ceiling is a magical thing without being too obvious and can affect how the space feels as well.

Parents often hear that reading to their children is critical for supporting development, and the message is getting through to them. In fact, in the United States, a little over half of children between the ages of three and five were read to every day in 2007, and 83% of children in that age group in the same country were read to three or more times per week in 2012.
This is good news, because reading to young children helps their language and brain development. In fact, recent research has found that both the quality and quantity of shared book reading in infancy predicted later childhood vocabulary and reading skills. In other words, the more time parents spend reading, the greater the developmental benefits in their four-year-old children.
This is an important finding. But does it matter what books parents read? A new study has investigated this question. It followed infants across the second six months of life and found that when parents showed babies books that had faces or objects with specific labels, they learned more. This is in contrast to books that did not name images, or books that had the same label under each image. Books that named different characters also promoted greater learning. So what does this mean for parents? Not all books are created equal, so parents need to choose the books they share with their children with great care.
